title: Chicken Teriyaki Donburi
description: Glossy soy-mirin chicken over rice. The sauce keeps the meat moist through three days of reheating, which is exactly what you want from a lunchbox.
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it by your usual method, then keep it covered.
Slice the chicken thighs into wide strips. Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat and brown the chicken hard on both sides, about 6 minutes.
Stir the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, garlic and ginger together, then pour into the pan.
Simmer 6 to 8 minutes, turning the chicken, until the sauce has reduced to a syrup that coats each piece.
Serve over the rice, scattered with spring onion and sesame seeds.
To store: divide rice and chicken into containers, sauce spooned over the top.

title: Thai Red Curry Chicken
description: A coconut curry that genuinely improves overnight as the paste settles into the sauce. Double it without changing anything.
steps: Start the rice.
Heat the oil in a deep pan and fry the curry paste for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant.
Add the chicken and turn it through the paste until coated and sealed.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a simmer and cook 12 minutes.
Add the capsicum and beans and cook a further 5 minutes, until just tender.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and lime juice. Serve over rice with coriander.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: Fast, high-protein and cheap. The broccoli softens by day two, so eat this one early in the week.
ingredients: 600 g beef rump steak, thinly sliced
steps: Start the rice. Whisk the oyster sauce, soy sauce, cornflour and water together.
Heat half the oil in a wok over the highest heat you have. Sear the beef in two batches so it browns rather than stews, about 2 minutes each. Set aside.
Add the rest of the oil, then the broccoli and a splash of water. Cover and steam 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce and toss until it thickens and turns glossy, about 1 minute. Serve over rice.

title: Japanese Beef Curry
description: Thick, mild and faintly sweet. Makes six serves from one pot and is arguably better on day three than on day one.
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck steak, cut into 3 cm cubes
steps: Brown the beef in the oil in batches in a heavy pot, then set aside.
Soften the onions in the same pot for 8 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder, flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Return the beef, pour in the stock and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook gently for 1 hour.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer uncovered another 30 minutes, until the beef pulls apart and the sauce coats a spoon.
Finish with honey and soy sauce. Serve with rice.

title: Korean Beef Bulgogi Bowls
description: Sweet-savoury marinated beef with rice and quick pickled cucumber. The beef and rice keep well; add the cucumber fresh.
ingredients: 700 g beef rump steak, thinly sliced
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and grated pear. Toss the beef through and leave 20 minutes while the rice cooks.
Toss the cucumber with the vinegar and a pinch of salt and set aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide pan over high heat and cook the beef in two batches, 2 to 3 minutes each, until caramelised at the edges.
Pile onto rice with the pickled cucumber, spring onion and sesame seeds.
To store: keep the cucumber in its own container so it stays crisp.

title: Thai Green Curry Chicken
description: Hotter and more herbal than the red curry, and just as forgiving of a few days in the fridge.
steps: Start the rice.
Fry the curry paste in the oil for 1 minute, then add the chicken and coat it well.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer 12 minutes.
Add the zucchini and beans and cook 5 minutes more.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and lime. Stir the basil through at the last moment and serve with rice.

title: Massaman Beef Curry
description: Mild, sweet and peanut-rich. A long slow pot that portions into six containers and reheats perfectly.
ingredients: 1 kg beef chuck steak, cut into cubes
steps: Fry the curry paste in a dry heavy pot for 2 minutes, then stir in half the coconut milk and simmer until it darkens and the oil separates.
Add the beef and turn it through the paste.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, cover and simmer very gently for 90 minutes.
Add the potatoes and onion and cook uncovered a further 30 minutes.
Stir in the peanut butter, fish sauce, sugar and tamarind. Taste: it should be sweet, salty and slightly sour at once.
Serve with rice.

title: Chinese Braised Soy Chicken
description: Chicken thighs braised in a dark, star-anise scented soy stock. One pot, almost no chopping.
steps: Put the drumsticks, soy sauce, sugar, stock, garlic, ginger and star anise in a pot. The liquid should come most of the way up the chicken.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook 35 minutes, turning the drumsticks once.
Uncover and simmer 10 minutes more so the sauce reduces and glazes.
Stir the sesame oil through off the heat. Serve on rice with spring onion and plenty of the braising liquid.

title: Vietnamese Caramel Pork
description: Sticky, salty-sweet braised pork. Deeply savoury, absurdly cheap, and one of the best leftovers on this list.
ingredients: 800 g pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
steps: Melt the sugar with a splash of water in a heavy pot over medium heat and let it darken to the colour of maple syrup. Watch it closely.
Stand back and add the fish sauce, then the garlic and ginger.
Add the pork and turn it through the caramel.
Pour in the water, cover and simmer 30 minutes, then uncover and reduce for 10 minutes until the sauce clings to the meat.
Grind over the pepper. Serve on rice with spring onion.

title: Chicken Fried Rice
description: The classic use for yesterday's rice — cold, dry grains fry properly where fresh ones steam.
steps: Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat and cook the chicken until browned. Set aside.
Scramble the eggs quickly in the same wok and set aside with the chicken.
Add the rest of the oil, then the onion and carrot, and stir-fry 4 minutes.
Add the cold rice and press it against the hot wok, turning every 30 seconds, until the grains separate and start to toast.
Return the chicken and egg, add the peas, soy sauce and oyster sauce, and toss until steaming.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

title: Mapo Tofu
description: Silky tofu and pork mince in a numbing chilli-bean sauce. Twenty minutes, and it reheats without any loss.
steps: Start the rice. Slide the tofu into a bowl of hot salted water to warm through while you cook.
Brown the pork mince hard in the oil, breaking it up as it goes.
Add the chilli bean paste, garlic and ginger and fry 1 minute until the oil turns red.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, then drain the tofu and add it. Simmer 5 minutes without stirring much — the cubes break easily.
Slake the cornflour in a little cold water and stir it through to thicken.
Serve on rice with sichuan pepper and spring onion.

title: Char Siu Pork
description: Lacquered barbecue pork. Roast a whole scotch fillet on Sunday and slice it into rice bowls, noodles and rolls all week.
steps: Mix everything except the pork and rice into a marinade. Reserve a third of it.
Cut the pork into two long strips and marinate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Roast the pork on a rack over a water-filled tray for 30 minutes.
Brush with the reserved marinade and roast a further 15 minutes until the edges char.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice across the grain. Serve with rice.

title: Beef Rendang
description: A dry, dark, intensely spiced curry that is traditionally made to keep. Two and a half hours of near-unattended simmering.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck steak, cut into cubes
steps: Fry the paste, onion, garlic and ginger in a heavy pot for 5 minutes.
Add the beef and turn it through until coated.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to a bare simmer and cook uncovered for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
As the liquid reduces the curry will darken and the oil will separate. Keep going for a further 30 minutes, stirring more often, until it is almost dry and the beef shreds under a spoon.
Season with sugar, tamarind and coriander. Serve with rice.

title: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowls
description: Fifteen minutes from pan to plate. Cooked fish is a next-day proposition at most, so plan one leftover lunch and no more.
steps: Start the rice. Steam the broccoli over it for the last 4 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, honey and ginger.
Fry the salmon skin-side down in the oil for 4 minutes, flip, and cook 2 minutes more.
Pour the sauce into the pan and let it bubble around the fish for a minute until syrupy.
Serve over rice with the broccoli, sesame seeds and spring onion.

title: Chicken Satay Skewers with Peanut Sauce
description: Skewers plus a peanut sauce that keeps for a week in a jar. Make the sauce once and use it three ways.
ingredients: 800 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into strips
steps: Toss the chicken with the curry powder and oil, then thread onto skewers.
Warm the peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce, sugar, lime juice and garlic in a small pot until smooth. Loosen with water to a pouring consistency.
Grill or pan-fry the skewers over high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until charred at the edges.
Serve with rice, cucumber and the peanut sauce.
To store: keep the sauce separate and warm it through when reheating.

title: Singapore Noodles
description: Curry-yellow rice vermicelli with prawns and pork. Reheats better than most noodle dishes because the noodles are barely sauced.
steps: Soak the rice noodles in hot water until pliable, then drain well.
Scramble the eggs in a little oil in a wok and set aside.
Fry the bacon until its fat renders, add the prawns and cook 2 minutes, then set aside.
Stir-fry the onion and capsicum for 3 minutes, then add the curry powder and cook 30 seconds.
Add the drained noodles and toss with the soy sauce until evenly yellow.
Return everything to the wok, finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

title: Mongolian Lamb
description: Sweet, dark and garlicky. Sear the lamb hard and keep the sauce reduced so it clings rather than pools.
steps: Toss the lamb in the cornflour. Start the rice.
Sear the lamb in two batches in a very hot wok, 2 minutes each, and set aside.
Fry the onion for 2 minutes, then the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the soy sauce, sugar and hoisin and let it bubble to a syrup.
Return the lamb, toss to coat, and add the spring onion at the last second. Serve on rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
description: Better than the takeaway version because the sauce is sharp rather than sugary. Reheat in the oven so the coating firms up again.
ingredients: 700 g pork shoulder, cut into cubes
steps: Toss the pork in the cornflour, shaking off the excess. Start the rice.
Shallow-fry the pork in the oil in batches until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper.
In the same pan, fry the capsicum and onion for 3 minutes.
Add the vinegar, sugar, tomato paste, soy sauce and water and simmer 5 minutes until glossy.
Return the pork with the pineapple and toss for 1 minute — no longer, or the coating softens. Serve with rice.

title: Chicken Laksa
description: Coconut laksa soup with poached chicken. Store the broth and the noodles apart or you will open the container to porridge.
steps: Fry the laksa paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and stock and bring to a simmer.
Slide in the chicken and poach gently for 10 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately and divide between bowls.
Season the broth with fish sauce and lime, then ladle over the noodles. Top with bean sprouts, coriander and spring onion.
To store: broth in one container, noodles in another.

title: Chicken Katsu Curry
description: Crumbed chicken with a mild curry sauce. The sauce keeps for days; the crumb wants an oven, not a microwave.
steps: Soften the onion and carrot in 1 tbsp of the oil for 8 minutes. Stir in the curry powder and the 2 tbsp flour and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in the stock and simmer 15 minutes, then blend smooth and season with soy sauce and honey.
Flatten the chicken breasts slightly. Coat each in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in the remaining oil for 4 minutes a side until deep golden and cooked through.
Slice and serve over rice with the sauce poured alongside.
To store: sauce and rice in the container, crumbed chicken on top, reheated in a hot oven.

title: Beef Bolognese
description: The archetypal batch-cook. Make a big pot on Sunday and it becomes pasta, a baked pasta, and a jacket potato filling.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil over low heat for 12 minutes. Do not rush this part.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the mince, and brown it hard, breaking it up.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes and stock, bring to a bare simmer and cook uncovered for 1 hour, until the sauce is thick and the fat has come to the surface.
Cook the spaghetti and toss it through the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Serve with parmesan.

title: Chicken Cacciatore
description: Chicken braised with tomatoes, olives and rosemary. A one-pot dish whose sauce protects the meat for days.
steps: Brown the chicken thighs in the oil in a wide pan, then set aside.
Soften the onion and capsicum in the same pan for 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Pour in the wine and scrape the base of the pan clean.
Add the tomatoes, olives, rosemary and capers, return the chicken, and simmer uncovered 40 minutes.
Serve over penne.

title: Lasagne al Forno
description: Eight serves from one tray, and it cuts more cleanly on day two than on the night. The definition of a batch meal.
steps: Make a ragù: soften the onion and carrot in the oil, add garlic, brown the mince, add tomato paste, wine and tomatoes, then simmer 45 minutes.
Make a béchamel: melt the butter, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the milk gradually and stir until thick. Season well.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Layer ragù, pasta sheets and béchamel three times, finishing with béchamel.
Scatter over both cheeses and bake 45 minutes until browned and bubbling.
Rest 15 minutes before cutting, or the layers slide.

title: Italian Meatballs in Tomato Sugo
description: Pork and beef meatballs simmered in tomato. They soak up more sauce every day they sit.
steps: Mix both minces with the breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, half the garlic and the parsley. Roll into 24 balls.
Brown them in the oil in batches, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan, add the remaining garlic, then the tomatoes and passata.
Return the meatballs, cover, and simmer 30 minutes.
Serve on spaghetti with more parmesan.

title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
description: Chicken in a garlic cream sauce with spinach and sundried tomato. Rich, fast, and a reliable weeknight fallback.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil in a wide pan, 5 minutes a side, then set aside.
Fry the garlic and sundried tomatoes for 1 minute.
Pour in the stock and cream and simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the chicken, add the spinach and let it wilt, then stir in the parmesan.
Serve over penne.

title: Minestrone Soup
description: A vegetable and bean soup that thickens overnight. Add the pasta to each bowl rather than the pot if you want it to survive the week.
ingredients: 400 g canned red kidney beans, drained
150 g green beans, cut into lengths
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the tomatoes and stock, bring to a simmer and cook 20 minutes.
Add the kidney beans, zucchini and green beans and simmer 10 minutes more.
Cook the pasta separately and add a spoonful to each bowl. Finish with parmesan.

title: Sausage and Fennel Rigatoni
description: Sausage meat crumbled into a tomato sauce with fennel seed. Six ingredients doing the work of twelve.
steps: Split the sausage skins and crumble the meat into a hot pan with the oil. Brown it well.
Add the onion and cook 6 minutes, then the garlic and fennel seeds for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir the cream through and season.
Toss with the cooked rigatoni and a splash of pasta water. Serve with parmesan.

title: Eggplant Parmigiana
description: Layered eggplant, tomato and mozzarella. A meat-free tray bake that sets firm in the fridge and reheats beautifully.
steps: Salt the eggplant slices and leave 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Brush with half the oil and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes until collapsing and golden.
Make a sauce: soften the onion in the remaining oil, add garlic, then the tomatoes, and simmer 20 minutes. Stir in the basil.
Layer eggplant, sauce, mozzarella and parmesan twice in a baking dish, finishing with the breadcrumbs and remaining parmesan.
Bake at 180°C for 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

title: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca
description: Anchovy, olive and caper sauce built entirely from the pantry. Twenty minutes and no shopping.
steps: Warm the oil with the anchovies, garlic and chilli flakes over low heat until the anchovies dissolve.
Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and simmer 15 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti and drain, keeping a cup of the water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with enough water to make it cling.
Finish with parsley. No cheese — the anchovies are doing that job.

title: Penne Arrabbiata
description: Garlic, chilli and tomato. Five ingredients, and the sauce doubles as a base for anything else in the fridge.
steps: Warm the oil with the garlic and chilli over low heat until the garlic turns pale gold. Do not let it brown.
Add the tomatoes, season, and simmer 15 minutes until thickened.
Cook the penne and toss it through the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Tear the basil over and serve with parmesan.

title: Tuna and Caper Spaghetti
description: Pantry pasta with tinned tuna, lemon and capers. Fifteen minutes on a night when nothing was planned.
steps: Cook the spaghetti, keeping a cup of the water.
Meanwhile warm the oil with the garlic and chilli until fragrant.
Flake in the tuna with the capers and lemon zest and warm through — do not fry it hard or it goes dry.
Toss the drained pasta through with the lemon juice and enough pasta water to loosen.
Finish with parsley.

title: Braised Beef Shin with Gremolata
description: Three hours of unattended braising turns the cheapest cut into the best meal of the week. Freezes and reheats without complaint.
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef shin, on the bone
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Brown the beef shin hard in the oil in a heavy casserole, then set aside.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery for 12 minutes, then add most of the garlic and the tomato paste.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes and stock.
Return the beef, cover, and braise in the oven for 3 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Mix the lemon zest, parsley and remaining garlic into a gremolata.
Serve over soft polenta with the gremolata scattered over.

title: Chicken Parmigiana
description: Crumbed chicken under tomato and cheese. Reheat in the oven — a microwave turns the crumb to paste.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C and roast the potato wedges in 1 tbsp of the oil for 40 minutes.
Butterfly the chicken breasts and flatten them. Coat in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in the remaining oil for 3 minutes a side until golden.
Warm the passata with the garlic and season.
Top each cutlet with sauce and both cheeses and bake 12 minutes until the cheese blisters.
Serve with the wedges.

title: Mushroom Risotto
description: Worth making, not worth storing: risotto sets solid and loses its texture overnight. Cook it for the night you eat it.
steps: Fry the mushrooms hard in the oil until browned and set aside.
Soften the onion in half the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Stir in the rice and toast it for 2 minutes until the edges turn translucent.
Add the wine and let it absorb, then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 20 minutes.
When the rice is just tender, beat in the remaining butter, the parmesan and the mushrooms.
Rest 2 minutes, then serve with parsley.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
description: Egg, cheese and cured pork, emulsified by pasta water. The sauce splits on reheating, so this is a same-night dish only.
steps: Fry the bacon in the oil over medium heat until its fat has rendered and the edges crisp.
Beat the eggs with the parmesan and a lot of black pepper.
Cook the spaghetti and drain it, keeping a cup of the water.
Off the heat, toss the hot pasta with the bacon and its fat, then the egg mixture, adding pasta water until it turns glossy.
Serve immediately. If the pan is too hot the egg scrambles.

title: Sausage and White Bean Stew
description: One pot, mostly pantry, and thick enough to eat with bread. Improves for three days.
steps: Brown the sausages whole in the oil, then set aside and cut into thick coins.
Soften the onion and carrot for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste.
Add the beans, tomatoes and stock and simmer 20 minutes, crushing a few beans against the side to thicken it.
Return the sausage and simmer 5 minutes.
Wilt the spinach through and finish with parsley.

title: Greek Chicken and Lemon Potato Tray Bake
description: Everything in one tray, no pans. The potatoes drink the lemon and chicken fat, which is the whole point.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Toss the potatoes, chicken and onion with the oil, lemon juice, garlic and oregano in a large roasting tray. Season heavily.
Pour the stock around the edges — it steams the potatoes from below while the tops roast.
Bake 40 minutes, turn everything, then bake a further 20 minutes until the potato edges catch.
Scatter over the feta and parsley.

title: Moussaka
description: Lamb, eggplant and cinnamon under a béchamel lid. Eight serves, and it slices far better cold than hot.
steps: Brush the eggplant with half the oil and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes.
Brown the lamb, then soften the onion and garlic in the same pan. Add the tomato paste, wine, tomatoes and cinnamon and simmer 30 minutes.
Make a béchamel with the butter, flour and milk, then beat in the eggs and half the parmesan off the heat.
Layer eggplant and lamb twice in a deep dish, then pour the béchamel over.
Scatter the remaining parmesan and bake at 180°C for 45 minutes until deep golden.
Rest 20 minutes before cutting.

title: Lamb Kleftiko
description: Lamb shoulder sealed in a parcel with lemon, garlic and oregano for three and a half hours. Almost no work, enormous reward.
ingredients: 1.8 kg lamb shoulder, on the bone
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Pierce the lamb all over and push slivers of garlic into the cuts.
Line a deep tray with two long sheets of baking paper and foil. Put the potatoes down first, then the lamb on top.
Pour over the lemon juice, oil and wine, and scatter the oregano and bay. Season hard.
Seal the parcel tightly and roast 3 hours.
Open the parcel, scatter the feta over and roast a final 30 minutes uncovered to colour the lamb.
Pull the meat apart with two forks and serve in its own juices.

title: Beef Stifado
description: Beef and whole baby onions braised with cinnamon, clove and red wine vinegar. A sweet-sour stew that peaks on day two.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck steak, cut into cubes
600 g pickling onions, peeled and left whole
steps: Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot in batches, then set aside.
Fry the whole onions until they colour on all sides, then add the garlic.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the wine and vinegar, and let it bubble for 2 minutes.
Return the beef with the tomatoes, spices, bay and stock.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours, until the beef gives way and the onions are whole but soft.
Fish out the cinnamon and bay before serving.

title: Pastitsio
description: The Greek baked pasta: cinnamon-spiced beef between tubes of pasta and a thick béchamel. Cuts into eight clean squares.
steps: Brown the mince, then soften the onion and garlic. Add the tomato paste, tomatoes and cinnamon and simmer 30 minutes until thick.
Cook the pasta two minutes short of done and toss with a little oil.
Make a thick béchamel with the butter, flour and milk. Off the heat beat in the eggs and half the parmesan.
Spread half the pasta in a deep dish, then all the meat, then the rest of the pasta.
Pour the béchamel over, scatter the remaining parmesan and bake at 180°C for 45 minutes.
Rest 20 minutes before cutting.

title: Keftedes in Tomato Sauce
description: Mint and oregano meatballs simmered in tomato. Serve with rice or bread; either way they keep three days.
steps: Mix both minces with the breadcrumbs, egg, grated onion, mint and oregano. Roll into 24 balls and chill 15 minutes.
Brown them in the oil in batches, then set aside.
Fry the garlic in the same pan, add the tomatoes and cinnamon, and simmer 10 minutes.
Return the meatballs and simmer gently 20 minutes.
Serve with rice.

title: Gigantes Plaki
description: Big butter beans baked in tomato with dill and honey. Meat-free, cheap, and as good cold as hot.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 12 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste.
Stir in the tomatoes and honey and simmer 10 minutes.
Fold the beans through, tip into a baking dish and bake 40 minutes until the top darkens and the sauce thickens.
Scatter over the herbs and feta.

title: Pork Souvlaki with Tzatziki
description: Lemon-oregano pork skewers with cucumber yoghurt. Keep the tzatziki in its own container and the meat reheats fine.
ingredients: 800 g pork shoulder, cut into cubes
steps: Marinate the pork in the oil, lemon juice, oregano and half the garlic for at least an hour.
Squeeze the water out of the grated cucumber, then mix with the yoghurt, dill and remaining garlic.
Thread the pork onto skewers and grill over high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until charred at the corners.
Warm the pita and serve with the pork, tzatziki, tomato and onion.

title: Avgolemono Chicken Soup
description: Chicken and rice soup thickened with egg and lemon. Reheat it gently — a hard boil curdles the egg.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the stock and chicken and simmer 20 minutes, then lift the chicken out and shred it.
Add the rice to the broth and cook 12 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the lemon juice, then ladle in hot broth a little at a time, whisking hard, to temper it.
Take the pot off the heat before stirring the egg mixture in, then return the chicken.
Finish with dill. Reheat over low heat only.

title: Briam
description: Slow-roasted summer vegetables in olive oil. Meat-free, keeps three days, and is arguably better at room temperature.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C.
Toss every vegetable with the garlic, oil, oregano and plenty of salt in the biggest tray you own.
Spread out so the pieces overlap rather than pile up.
Roast 45 minutes, turn everything, then roast a further 30 minutes until the edges blacken slightly.
Scatter over the parsley and feta.

title: Revithada Chickpea Stew
description: Chickpeas slow-baked with onion, lemon and rosemary until they collapse into their own broth. Almost nothing to it.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C.
Put the chickpeas, onion, oil, garlic, rosemary, bay and stock in a casserole and season well.
Cover and bake 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake a further 25 minutes so the top browns and the liquid reduces to a loose sauce.
Stir in the lemon juice and parsley just before serving.

title: Spanakopita
description: Spinach and feta between filo. Reheat in the oven only — the microwave turns the pastry to wet paper.
steps: Wilt the spinach in a dry pan, then squeeze out as much water as you physically can. This step decides whether the base is crisp or soggy.
Soften the onion in the oil, then mix with the spinach, spring onion, dill, both cheeses and the eggs.
Heat the oven to 180°C. Brush 6 filo sheets with butter and layer them in a tray, letting the edges overhang.
Spread the filling, then fold the overhang in and top with 6 more buttered sheets.
Score the top into squares and bake 50 minutes until deep gold.
Rest 15 minutes before cutting through.

title: Greek Salad with Grilled Chicken
description: Eaten cold, so it makes an easy next-day lunch — but only one. Dressed salad does not last a second night.
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the oil, half the lemon juice and the oregano, then grill 6 minutes a side. Rest and slice.
Combine the tomato, cucumber, onion and olives in a wide bowl.
Whisk the remaining oil, lemon juice and vinegar and pour over.
Lay the feta on top in slabs rather than crumbling it, and add the chicken.
To store: keep the dressing separate and add it the moment you eat.
